metadata.note: The pre-1869 constituents of the Lake Shore and Michigan Southern west of Toledo: the Erie and Kalamazoo (Toledo - Adrian, steam from 1837), the State of Michigan's Southern Railroad (Monroe - Adrian 1840, Hillsdale 1843; sold 9 May 1846), the Michigan Southern Rail Road (1846-1855, which reached Chicago in 1852) and the Michigan Southern and Northern Indiana (25 Apr 1855 - 6 Apr 1869). One feature per drawable span and operator, split at each ownership change (Rule 4), on geometry shared with the LS&MS layer's features of the same corridors. Every corridor continues from 1869 in lake_shore_and_michigan_southern_railway.geojson.
metadata.colour: Four new company colours, none used by any company anywhere in data/ (checked programmatically 2026-11-03 with names normalised): Erie and Kalamazoo #7D6B3A, Southern Railroad of Michigan #4F7A6B, Michigan Southern #B05A7A, Michigan Southern and Northern Indiana #9C5BA5. The last two are in the plum family of the successor LS&MS #8E4A7A and distinct from it and from New York Central #5C677D.
metadata.company_names: 'Southern Railroad of Michigan' is the display name chosen for the State of Michigan's Southern Railroad (1840-1846), to keep it distinct from every other 'Southern Railroad'. 'Michigan Southern' is the Michigan Southern Rail Road (1846-1855).
metadata.ownership_split: Splits drawn: 9 May 1846 State (Southern Railroad of Michigan) -> Michigan Southern on Monroe - Adrian and Adrian - Hillsdale; 1 Aug 1849 Erie and Kalamazoo -> Michigan Southern (lessee) on Toledo - Adrian (1844 per michiganrailroads - CONFLICT, 1844-1849 undrawn); 25 Apr 1855 Michigan Southern -> MS&NI everywhere; 6 Apr 1869 MS&NI -> LS&MS (the other layer). Era boundaries share a year, as elsewhere in the repo. NOT splits: the 1 Jul 1856 DM&T lease (before the DM&T opened - drawn as MS&NI throughout); the Michigan Southern's purchase of St. Joseph Valley stock.
metadata.omitted: Per the report's drawable fields: [1] Toledo - Adrian 1844-1849 (operator unresolved between the E&K and the Michigan Southern - NONE); [6] the Chicago approach 1852-1866 (IC lakefront vs Rock Island via Englewood unresolved - NONE; main line stops at Grand Crossing for those years); [12] Palmyra - Tecumseh 1838-1855 under the Palmyra and Jacksonburgh, the State Tecumseh branch and the Michigan Southern (no evidence of trains; 1838 motive power unknown, Rule 5) - NONE; [13] Tecumseh - Clinton 1853-1855 (track only) - NONE; [14] Detroit, Monroe and Toledo as its own operator - NONE; [15] Northern Indiana as its own operator 1851-1855 - NONE; [16] White Pigeon - Constantine (no passenger year) - NONE; [17] St. Joseph Valley / Schoolcraft and Three Rivers / Kalamazoo and Schoolcraft (not MS&NI-operated) - NONE; [18] Kalamazoo, Allegan and Grand Rapids (operator unresolved; LS&MS layer covers 1869) - NONE; [19] Michigan City Branch (no passenger year) - NONE; [20] Rock Island stock / joint depot / lake steamers - NONE.
metadata.freight_only_check: No freight-only line drawn. White Pigeon - Constantine and the Michigan City Branch are omitted as unsourced (no confirmed passenger year), not as freight.
metadata.horsecar_check: Rule 5: the Erie and Kalamazoo is drawn from 1837 (steam locomotive 'Adrian'), not from the horse-drawn opening of 18 Aug / 2 Nov 1836. The Palmyra and Jacksonburgh (1838, power unknown) is not drawn at all.
conflicts: Erie and Kalamazoo lease to the Michigan Southern: 1 Aug 1849 (Wikipedia LS&MS) vs 1844 (michiganrailroads E&K page; 'Crossing the Mitten'). E&K drawn to 1844, Michigan Southern from 1849, 1844-1849 undrawn.

Chicago approach 1852-1866: IC lakefront (Fowler IN 20A) vs Rock Island via Englewood from 1853 (Wikipedia LS&MS; michiganrailroads 1853 joint Van Buren depot; Fowler's own Englewood 'Chicago Junction x' 1858). Undrawn; 1866-1869 via Englewood drawn.
Air Line opening: May 1857 (michiganrailroads [LS]) vs completed 1858 (Wikipedia). Drawn 1858.
Detroit - Monroe opening: Dec 1855 [AAD] vs Dec 1856 [EMR4] vs scheduled trains Jan 1857. Monroe - Toledo: first train 25 Dec 1856 (Wikipedia) vs official opening Oct 1857 [EMR4]. Drawn 1857.
Monroe - Adrian: Petersburg 1839 vs first train 23 Nov 1840 [MCR-75]; Adrian Dec 1839 [AAD] vs 1840 (Wikipedia). Drawn 1840; 1841 not excluded.
Jonesville: Sep 1850 [MCR-75] vs 1849 (Hillsdale station page). Drawn 1850.
Erie and Kalamazoo steam: 4 Jul 1837 (michiganrailroads [MDOT]) vs Aug 1837 (Wikipedia). Same year.
not_yet_sourced: WHO RAN THE TRAINS IN INDIANA 1851-1855 (ms-white-pigeon-south-bend, ms-south-bend-grand-crossing): drawn as Michigan Southern at LOW confidence, as the report recommends; the Northern Indiana and Chicago may have run its own trains. Bogle, 'Railroad Building in Indiana, 1850-1855' (Indiana Magazine of History) is the place to look.
Toledo - Adrian 1844-1849: operator unresolved (lease-date conflict); undrawn.
Chicago approach 1852-1866: undrawn pending the IC vs Rock Island question.
Date the Jackson Branch junction moved from Palmyra to Lenawee Junction (no later than 1868) - the drawn Lenawee Junction start may be later than its era for part of 1855-1867.

No timetable between the 1858 Dinsmore Guide and the 1868 Official Guide was seen; 1859-1867 MS&NI spans assume continuity. [OG-1868] itself is read through a michiganrailroads summary, not the Guide.

1840s State / Michigan Southern continuity between the 1843 Hillsdale opening and the Nov 1850 '68 miles in operation' rests on the 1846 sale and Fowler's undefined '1847SG' tags; state-era motive power assumed steam.

Monroe Pier (msni-monroe-pier): drawn as an 1856 [ANCHOR] only - service certainly ran wider both ways (the Michigan Southern's Buffalo - Monroe steamers predate 1855) but no other year is confirmed, and no end date was found. Whether the 1856 pier stood exactly at the drawn OHM way's eastern end is not verified.
Fowler MI 172's 64.3 mi Detroit - Toledo vs the 57.1 mi drawn (inherited from lsms-detroit-toledo).
Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh in this layer is an estimate.
metadata.geometry_sources: All geometry is cut from lake_shore_and_michigan_southern_railway.geojson (lsms-old-road, lsms-main-toledo-chicago, lsms-detroit-toledo, lsms-monroe-branch, lsms-jackson-branch), which was routed with opstrace.py over OSM (old_railway_operator=NYC) and OHM on 2026-10-30. Cut points were snapped to the nearest existing vertex from Nominatim geocodes whose type was checked (Hillsdale, Elkhart and Monroe returned counties and were hand-pinned); Grand Crossing is a vertex inserted at the main line's crossing of the IC main line as drawn in metra.geojson. Exception: msni-monroe-pier is OpenHistoricalMap way 198758506 (unnamed, railway=rail, start_date 1839, end_date 1975), east of the Monroe branch's Monroe point, read from an OHM Overpass fetch on 2026-11-03. One straight connector (0.4 mi, Lenawee Junction) joins the Monroe branch to the Old Road. Every feature therefore draws the LS&MS-era / surviving alignment, which is LATER than its own era - stated per feature.
metadata.existing_layer_findings: Confirmed the report's EXISTING LAYER CHECK: no feature anywhere in data/ draws a pre-1869 segment for any of these four companies, and none of the four company names had a colour. The LS&MS features' 1869 starts are company boundaries and were not changed.

properties.geometry_quality: No straight-line approximated legs: 33.5 mi drawn against 32.4 mi documented (Fowler MI 174, Toledo 0.0 - Adrian 32.4). Cut from lsms-old-road between its Toledo start and the vertex nearest Adrian (0.7 km from the Adrian geocode). Toledo - Sylvania - Blissfield follows OpenHistoricalMap's unnamed grade (lifted); Blissfield - Adrian the surviving Adrian and Blissfield track. ALIGNMENT ERA (Rule 2): drawn on the LS&MS-era geometry of lsms-old-road - the surviving or last-known alignment as mapped in OSM/OHM, NOT a survey of the 1837-1844 line. Any relocation, double-tracking or curve easing made after 1837 is drawn as if it had always been there. The Toledo end is the LS&MS layer's hand-pin near the later Union Station site: a LATER terminal and entry than this era's. The Erie and Kalamazoo entered Toledo by street running to Monroe/Water Streets; the Michigan Southern replaced that in the 1850s with an east-west tangent over Swan Creek (michiganrailroads 1836 [AATHS]) - neither the street-running entry nor the original depot is drawn. The E&K was 4 ft 10 in gauge until regauged in 1848 - gauge is not drawn. The line is drawn through Lenawee Junction, where the later Jackson Branch connection was made; the original 1838 Palmyra and Jacksonburgh junction was at Palmyra, 0.7 km from the drawn line.

segments.note: Report block [1]: Toledo - Sylvania - Ottawa Lake - Riga - Blissfield - Palmyra - Adrian. Drawn from 1837, when the steam locomotive 'Adrian' replaced horses (Aug 1837 per Wikipedia LS&MS; 4 Jul 1837 per michiganrailroads 1837 [MDOT] - same year). Rule 5: the horse-drawn service of 18 Aug 1836 (Toledo - Palmyra) / 2 Nov 1836 (Toledo - Adrian) is NOT drawn. First railroad mail contract west of the Alleghenies 3 Jan 1839 (michiganrailroads 1839 [EMR4]) shows operation in 1839. END 1844 is the earlier side of a SOURCE CONFLICT on the Michigan Southern lease: 1 Aug 1849 (Wikipedia LS&MS) vs 1844 (michiganrailroads E&K company page; 'Crossing the Mitten'). The E&K's own era is drawn only to the earlier date; 1844-1849 is left undrawn because its operator is unresolved - this is a withheld unknown, not an end of service. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 1440 (one train each way a day) is an ESTIMATE - no timetable of this era was seen (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: this segment's own note names the source for its start year (Wikipedia LS&MS; michiganrailroads 1837) and its end year (the 1844 lease date, michiganrailroads E&K page - in conflict with Wikipedia's 1849) (via the MS&NI branch research report, research/branches/michigan_southern_and_northern_indiana_railroad.txt, researched 2026-11-03); its headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Report block [11]: Monroe City - Monroe Pier, the boat-train track to the Lake Erie dock of the company's Buffalo - Monroe steamers (Southern Michigan, Northern Indiana). [ANCHOR]: the only evidence is Fowler MI 173's 'Monroe Pier 1856t' (an 1856 company public timetable). Service certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year is confirmed - do not widen this anchor to look plausible, and do not delete it to tidy the map. Pier traffic presumably faded once the Detroit and Toledo lines opened (1857); no end date was found. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (Rule 3).
